Night Of Thunder was lucky to be born at all, even more than all of us who are plucked out of the ether to come into existence. Bred by the late retail magnate Frank Dunne, he was the only offspring of the Listed-placed Galileo mare Forest Storm, who had failed to get in foal to Clodovil two years earlier and was barren again to Dalakhani in 2012, when she died.

Night Of Thunder also has far from perfect foreleg conformation, ‘toeing out’ quite markedly, so was doomed to fetch a small price. In reality, it’s fortunate that he remained in a major racing nation at all. The next cheapest lot by Dubawi at Tattersalls October Book 1 that year was sold to compete in Ukraine.

As it turned out, Night Of Thunder entered training with Richard Hannon snr during his last season with his name on the licence at East Everleigh, and carried the white silks with red sash of Saeed Manana made famous by the siblings Luso, Needle Gun and Warrsan.

He won both his starts at two by wide margins, including the Listed Doncaster Stakes, to establish himself as an exciting three-year-old prospect for 2014.

## Background

Night of Thunder is a chestnut colt with a white star and two white socks bred in Ireland by Frank Dunne. He was sired by Dubawi, a top-class son of Dubai Millennium, whose wins included the Irish 2,000 Guineas and the Prix Jacques Le Marois. At stud, Dubawi has been a highly successful breeding stallion, siring major winners such as Monterosso, Al Kazeem, Makfi, Lucky Nine, and Poet's Voice.

As a yearling, Night of Thunder was sent to the Tattersalls sales, where he was bought for 32,000 guineas by representatives of Rabbah Bloodstock. Night of Thunder entered into the ownership of Saeed Manana and was sent into training with Richard Hannon Sr. at East Everleigh in Wiltshire.
